text:
maria: FYI saw a 30-40% throughput drop on the nf4+fp4 rollout this morning, coincident with a burst of small requests. suspect sample-rate adaptation + batching heuristics interaction causing KV pressure.

josh: which hosts / deploy id?

maria: deploy id rwd-td-4q; affected pool eu-west-2-gpu-a, ~18 hosts. spike started at 09:12 UTC. p95 latency doubled for short seq (<=64). logs show frequent small microbatches and host->device memcpy spikes.

sophia: are you seeing increased KV evictions?

maria: yes — kv eviction rate jumped from ~0.7/s to 12/s. memory used by KV slab also shows fragmentation delta. attached short stack of perf counters.

runtime-bot: ALERT rwd-td-4q: model nf4-fp4:v12 throughput drop detected (scope=eu-west-2-gpu-a) — rolling window 10m, loss=34%

josh: can you paste the telemetry sample-rate config? maybe sampler started up-weighting short requests.

maria: here are relevant flags we flipped for adaptive sampling last week:

```
adaptive_sampling.enabled = true
adaptive_sampling.min_sample_rate = 0.01
adaptive_sampling.max_sample_rate = 0.5
adaptive_sampling.window = "30s"
heuristics.batch_min = 2
heuristics.batch_max_delay_ms = 8
kv.prefetch_enabled = true
```

maria: telemetry shows sample_rate for short-path rose from 0.02 -> 0.42 before the throughput drop.

sophia: so sampler increased short requests visibility which caused the scheduler to favor microbatching for short seqs -> many small batches -> KV cache warmed/pinned differently?

devin: microbatching alone shouldn't cause mem spikes — what about hybrid quant kernel selection? were we switching kernels at runtime based on seq length?

maria: yes, selector was toggling between nf4-4bit-fast and nf4-4bit-stable kernels depending on latency window. kernel-switch count spiked. logs: "kernel_select: swap nf4-4bit-fast -> nf4-4bit-stable (reason=latency_window)" repeated. each swap triggers KV state reconcile and partial cache rebuild on device.

anya: that explains percent of host->device memcpy spikes — kernel switch path copies KV fragments to new layout briefly. if happening across many requests you get thrash.

josh: can we confirm eviction pattern aligns with kernel switches? grep kernel_select and kv_eviction in logs.

maria: quick grep output (snip):

```
09:11:58 kernel_select: fast->stable req_id=... host=10.1.3.14
09:11:59 kv_eviction: slab_frag=0.12 req_id=...
09:12:03 kernel_select: stable->fast req_id=... host=10.1.3.14
09:12:04 kv_eviction: slab_frag=0.18 req_id=...
```

maria: sequence shows switch -> eviction -> switch -> eviction in tight loop.

sophia: immediate mitigation: pin kernel choice per-host for a grace period and disable adaptive sampling ramp for short-path. that should stop thrash.

josh: agree. also consider delaying kernel switch until KV quiet or use non-blocking rebind.

devin: I've got a quick patch to make kernel-switch be no-copy for stable->fast if layouts compatible. can push to canary in 10m.

runtime-bot: DEPLOY_START user=devin target=eu-west-2-gpu-a canary_hosts=2 commit=patch/kv-nocopy-2026

maria: until patch lands, I'll flip `adaptive_sampling.max_sample_rate=0.05` on that pool and set `heuristics.batch_min=4` to force larger batches.

deploy-bot: completed config update for rwd-td-4q on eu-west-2-gpu-a (changed adaptive_sampling.max_sample_rate => 0.05, heuristics.batch_min => 4).

josh: good. can you also capture perf counters for memcpy, kernel_switch_count, kv_evictions pre/post? want a small table for postmortem.

maria: collecting now, will post a short diff in ~15m. initial glance after deploy: p95 for short seq down ~45% from peak, eviction rate down to 1.1/s. memcpy spikes still occasionally but much lower.

anya: long-term: we should add hysteresis to kernel selection and prefer in-place layout-compatible swaps. also add a check in sampler: avoid ramping sample rate when kernel_switch_count > X in window.

sophia: and add metric: "kernel_switch_kv_cost" to alert before rollout triggers global evictions.

devin: implemented no-copy path in PR, will post diffs + microbench numbers once CI passes. local microbench shows 0.7x memcpy and 1.12x throughput improvement for mixed short/long workload.

maria: thanks. created a tracking issue: https://internal/issues/RWD-1108 (4-bit rollout: sampler + kernel-switch hysteresis). tagging infra for follow-up.

josh: thanks team. action items: (1) peter to review PR (devin), (2) sophia/anya iterate hysteresis + metrics, (3) maria to run 2h canary and post perf counters.

maria: quick note — if anyone hits the pool while I'm running canary, please message me before toggling sampling. :raised_hands:

runtime-bot: DEPLOY_SUCCESS user=devin target=eu-west-2-gpu-a canary_hosts=2 commit=patch/kv-nocopy-2026 duration=210s

maria: canary looks stable at +2h. I'll schedule a gradual ramp for the rest of the pool tomorrow at low traffic window.

josh: nice find — this pattern could have shown up only with nf4/fp4 mixed kernels and the adaptive sampler. documenting now.

maria: posting perf counters (short diff):

```
metric                 before     after
p95_latency_ms         142         78
kv_evictions_per_s     12.3        1.1
kernel_switchs_per_min 28          3
host_to_device_mb/s    230         68
```

maria: saving logs to /var/log/redwood/rollouts/rwd-td-4q/2362345678-logs.tar.gz

anya: filing followups against RWD-1108. moving to postmortem board. :white_check_mark:
